target_customer: Payments platforms, ISOs, PayFacs and sponsor banks; originally fintechs underwriting SMBs
problem: Traditional bureaus cover small businesses poorly, so risk shows up only at chargebacks or defaults; merchant risk operations are manual.
business_model: B2B SaaS/API for merchant risk underwriting, monitoring and fraud detection

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating unstructured SMB web data and building risk models is standard data engineering with hard modeling parts.

defensibility.rationale: Data and workflow integrations help, but risk tooling markets have many vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: VentureBeat says incumbents were slow to adopt NLP; no acquisition or copy found.

market_need_then: YC launch post says bureau SMB coverage is poor, integrations painful and data unstructured; founders spent 20+ years in payments risk.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and confident, outcome-focused ('building the trust layer for commerce')

brand_strength.rationale: Short invented name; no brand-specific evidence.

pivots.from: Risk API with alternative data and monitoring for fintechs underwriting SMBs
pivots.to: AI risk platform for payments platforms, ISOs, PayFacs and sponsor banks (agents, transaction monitoring, ForgeCheck)
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from the YC launch post versus the current site

outcome_analysis: Coris is active, claims customers such as GoFundMe, Kajabi, Clio and HubSpot, and raised a $3.7M seed in February 2024 co-led by Lux and Exponent. Founders from PayPal, WePay and eBay give strong founder-market fit. Its product expanded from an SMB data API to a broader AI risk platform, but revenue and later rounds are not public.
